issues.reason: The candidate constrains the object to the class nltl:iceClassValue, but sh:class does not restrict the value to the six specific source-defined classes. Consequently, an additional iceClassValue instance could satisfy the shape. The candidate itself states that enumeration is not constrained.
issues.expected: The representation should restrict nltl:iceClass values to the six source-defined classes, if canonical mapped individuals or an equivalent supplied closed-set representation is available.
issues.suggestion: Provide canonical mappings for IA Super, IA, IB, IC, II, and III, then add a closed-set constraint such as sh:in using those mapped values. Do not invent individual IRIs from the current evidence.
issues.candidate_excerpt:
sh:class nltl:iceClassValue ;
        sh:message "A ship must be assigned exactly one ice-class value. Clause 1.8 defines the controlled value set as ice class IA Super, IA, IB, IC, II, and III; canonical IRIs for those individual values were not supplied, so enumeration cannot be constrained here without inventing IRIs."@en

issues.reason: Clause 1.8 says that ships are assigned to ice classes, but the supplied source and schema do not expressly establish that the RDF property must have exactly one value. The singular wording may describe the legal assignment without resolving RDF cardinality, and no ontology cardinality restriction or approved representation rule is supplied.
issues.expected: The cardinality of nltl:iceClass should remain unresolved unless an approved representation rule confirms that every ship must have exactly one value.
issues.suggestion: Confirm the intended RDF cardinality for nltl:iceClass. Retain sh:minCount 1 and sh:maxCount 1 only if exactly-one representation is approved; otherwise revise or remove those constraints.

No cardinality restriction for <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#iceClass> is present in the supplied ontology evidence.
issues.source_excerpt:
Under section 3 of the Act on the Ice Classes of Ships and Icebreaker Assistance (1121/2005),
ships are assigned to ice classes as follows:

unchecked: The qualitative eligibility conditions for each class—structure, engine output, navigation capability, ice severity, icebreaker assistance, steel hull, open-sea fitness, and own propulsion—are not represented by the supplied schema paths and were not assessed as enforceable RDF constraints.
Whether the six class descriptions are intended as independently validated classification criteria or only as controlled labels remains unresolved.

Canonical individual IRIs or an equivalent supplied mapping for IA Super, IA, IB, IC, II, and III were not supplied, so the required closed-set constraint cannot be completed without additional mapping context.

The applicability statement in section 1.1 that sections 1.8 and chapter 2 apply to all ships irrespective of year of build was not modeled because the supplied requirement is limited to clause 1.8 and the declared representation scope.
